column7: ADR-112 gave upgraded deployments that never set security.require_mfa a grace period with no end condition: applyADR112UpgradeGrace set RequireMFA=false for the whole boot and only an explicit key ended it, so such a deployment could stay unenforced forever with only a start-up warning. Now the grace period ends at the first global admin-tier holder with a second factor (TOTP or passkey) or 30 days after the durably recorded start (system_metadata adr112.require_mfa.grace_started, written once by the first graced boot), whichever comes first, while the server runs: every MFA gate (core session issuance, server/middleware.EnforceAccountSetupLive, the gRPC unary/stream interceptors, auth-config) reads core.KeyorixCore.MFARequired per request; the end latches and writes adr112.require_mfa.enforced. Users without a second factor are then confined to MFA enrolment, never locked out. Proving test: the real router over a real core, an admin and a user sign in without MFA during the grace period (mfa_grace on login/profile, no 403), the admin enrols TOTP over HTTP, and the same user session is then refused 403 MFAEnrollmentRequired everywhere except the enrolment endpoints; red when the gate is frozen at the boot value. Siblings: TestMFAGrace_DeadlineEnforces, TestAuthInterceptor_MFAUpgradeGrace (gRPC), TestMFAUpgradeGrace_* (core, SQLite + Postgres).
